title: RCMP shooting victim's family suing officers
subtitle: Shotgun-wielding man was out to scare vandals, widow says
article: The widow and extended family of a God's Lake Narrows man shot and killed two years ago by police as he approached them while carrying a shotgun are suing the federal justice department and two RCMP officers over his death, alleging the cops mistook him for a threat and were reckless and negligent when they opened fire without warning.

Olive Duck, 55, has filed claim for unspecified financial damages in the Court of Queen's Bench as a judicial inquest into the March 15, 2011 early morning fatal shooting of Paul Leonard Duck, 52, winds its way towards public hearings.
In an inquest notification, the province says Duck died of a gunshot wound to his arm. He was shot by two RCMP officers who were approached by a group, including Duck, who was carrying a gun.
At the time, the officers were guarding the scene of a fatal house fire. They heard gunshots and the sound of glass breaking near where they were and had called for assistance, the province says.
Olive Duck says her husband went armed with a shotgun and four shells to a home being vandalized by youth -- but claims they both tried to contact RCMP before he went there.
On arrival, Paul Duck yelled verbal warnings to the vandals to clear off and fired three shotgun blasts into the air, Olive says in her claim. When they fled, her husband followed them, she says.
He encountered the Mounties and approached them for help, she says.
"He was holding the shotgun across his body and at waist level insuring (sic) it was not pointed at (the officers)," Olive claims.
One of the officers fired three shots at him, striking him twice, without asking why he had the gun or warning him to drop it, the lawsuit alleges.
The officers are accused -- among other things -- of failing to use the skill expected of an RCMP officer to assess and defuse the situation and using excessive force.
The allegations have not been proven nor tested in court and no statement of defence has been filed.
